concepts.name: Queries by role and accessible name

questions.prompt: A visible submit button has the accessible name Save. Which query best reflects its user-facing identity?

choices.text: getByTestId because IDs always outrank semantics.
querySelector for its fourth nested wrapper element.
getByText on a CSS class name hidden from users.
getByRole with button and name Save.

questions.explanation: Role and accessible name reflect how users and assistive technology identify the control. IDs and DOM position couple the test to implementation.

sources.title: Testing Library: About Queries
sources.claim: Testing Library prioritizes role and accessible-name queries over test IDs when semantic queries are available.

questions.prompt: A test must assert that an error message is absent. Which query avoids throwing just because it is missing?

choices.text: findByText, which synchronously returns undefined.
getAllByText, which never fails when nothing matches.
queryByText.
getByText, which returns null on absence.

questions.explanation: queryBy supports absence checks by returning null. getBy throws, while findBy waits for a match.

sources.title: Testing Library: About Queries
sources.claim: getBy throws on absence, queryBy returns null on absence, and findBy retries asynchronously; singular queries reject multiple matches.

questions.prompt: A waitFor callback returns false until a result appears, but the test does not retry as intended. What is needed?

choices.text: Ignore the callback result and end the test early.
Throw through an assertion until the condition holds.
Return a different false value on every attempt.
Use a fixed sleep instead of checking the condition.

questions.explanation: waitFor retries when the callback throws. Merely returning a falsy value does not request a retry.

sources.title: Testing Library async methods
sources.claim: waitFor retries a callback when it throws and findBy waits for an element; asynchronous utilities must be awaited.

questions.prompt: Why prefer user-event typing over dispatching only a single low-level input event?

choices.text: It models the sequence of a user interaction.
It disables the need to assert the resulting UI state.
It guarantees the real browser sends a production request.
It bypasses visibility checks to interact with hidden controls.

questions.explanation: user-event models interactions rather than one event dispatch. Tests still need assertions, and simulated interaction does not establish production behavior.

sources.title: Introduction to user-event
sources.claim: user-event simulates complete interactions with visibility and interactability checks and recommends setup before interaction.

questions.prompt: A form contains Save and Cancel buttons. Which query identifies Save through accessible semantics?

choices.text: getByRole("button") while assuming only the first is returned.
Select the first button regardless of its accessible name.
Query a hidden CSS class that happens to contain Save.
getByRole("button", { name: "Save" }).

questions.explanation: The name option disambiguates the role. A singular query with two matches fails; DOM order is a weaker implementation detail.

sources.title: Testing Library: About Queries
sources.claim: Role queries can include an accessible name to distinguish similar controls.

questions.prompt: A success banner appears after a submitted request completes. Which lookup fits the timing?

choices.text: getByText before submitting the request.
findByText without awaiting its pending promise.
await findByText for the success banner.
queryByText once, treating null as proof the request finished.

questions.explanation: findBy retries until the banner appears or times out. Immediate checks can race, and an unawaited promise does not establish completion.

sources.title: Testing Library: About Queries
sources.claim: findBy waits for an element and returns a promise.

questions.prompt: Which query practices follow Testing Library priorities? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A singular role query returns the first of several matching buttons by default.
Query an exposed button by role and accessible name.
Use a label-based query for a labelled form field.
Prefer test IDs even when an appropriate role query is available.
Treat wrapper nesting as the public contract of a component.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: Singular queries reject multiple matches; use a distinguishing accessible name. B is correct: Semantic queries reflect user-facing behavior. C is correct: Labels are a direct way users identify fields. D is incorrect: Test IDs have lower priority than accessible queries. E is incorrect: DOM structure is an implementation detail.

sources.title: Testing Library: About Queries
sources.claim: Testing Library prioritizes role and accessible-name queries over test IDs when semantic queries are available.

questions.prompt: Which singular-query behaviors are documented? Select all that apply.

choices.text: getBy throws when no matching element exists.
queryBy returns null when no matching element exists.
findBy returns a promise that retries for a match.
queryBy returns the first element when several elements match.
findBy is a synchronous alias for queryBy.

questions.explanation: A is correct: Immediate absence is an error for getBy. B is correct: This supports assertions of absence. C is correct: It combines query behavior with waiting. D is incorrect: A singular query throws on multiple matches. E is incorrect: Its asynchronous waiting behavior is distinct.

sources.title: Testing Library: About Queries
sources.claim: getBy throws on absence, queryBy returns null on absence, and findBy retries asynchronously; singular queries reject multiple matches.

questions.prompt: Which choices support reliable asynchronous DOM tests? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Make waitFor callbacks throw while their expected condition is unmet.
Return false as the required signal for waitFor to retry.
waitFor executes its callback only once regardless of thrown assertions.
Use the same fixed sleep as proof that every UI update completed.
Await findBy when a matching element appears after an update.

questions.explanation: A is correct: A thrown error triggers retry. B is incorrect: Falsy return alone does not cause a retry. C is incorrect: It retries a throwing callback until success or timeout. D is incorrect: Elapsed time is not a condition-based assertion. E is correct: The query waits for the element.

sources.title: Testing Library async methods
sources.claim: waitFor retries a callback when it throws and findBy waits for an element; asynchronous utilities must be awaited.

questions.prompt: Which user-event practices match the guide? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Treat one fireEvent dispatch as equivalent to every full interaction.
Expect normal typing to bypass hidden or disabled controls.
Assert the visible behavior produced by the interaction.
Create a user instance with userEvent.setup in the test flow.
Await asynchronous user interactions such as typing.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: Real interactions often require multiple events and checks. B is incorrect: user-event performs visibility and interactability checks. C is correct: Simulation alone does not prove the outcome. D is correct: The setup API provides the interaction session. E is correct: Interactions can involve multiple asynchronous steps.

sources.title: Introduction to user-event
sources.claim: user-event simulates complete interactions with visibility and interactability checks and recommends setup before interaction.
